## What the check enforces

An activation audit (`plans:audit { phase:'activation' }`) has always checked the FORWARD direction: every requirement the owner stated maps to a plan target. It now also checks the REVERSE direction. Every current, non-dropped plan item must resolve to exactly one of:

| label | meaning | GUI chip |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | at least one source ref of a mapping that targets the item is an owner turn | Yours |
| `derived` | declared as following from targets that are themselves owner-backed | Derived from P-001, R-2 |
| `agent-added` | declared as the agent's own addition, with a reason the owner can read | Agent-added |
| `unresolved` | none of the above; the chip names why | `Unresolved: <reason>` |

The GUI shows `Not audited` for an item added after the latest audit.

Only the turn-origin verdicts `owner-typed`, `owner-turn` and `owner-dialog` count as the owner (`OWNER_TURN_VERDICTS` in `packages/operator-core/lib/activation-item-provenance.ts`). An assistant turn, a machine-injected turn (a wake, loop fire, compaction continuation or coord inject), and an unknown-origin turn never count on their own. A mapping may still cite them as context, as long as it also cites an owner turn. A mapping whose disposition is `rejected` does not make its targets owner-backed.

## Declaring the items no owner turn backs

Pass `itemProvenance` on the activation audit:

```json
{ "itemProvenance": [
  { "itemId": "P-006", "kind": "derived", "from": ["P-001", "R-2"] },
  { "itemId": "P-007", "kind": "agent-added", "reason": "Docs are how the next agent finds the rule." }
] }
```

Declarations carry forward across re-audits by `itemId`, so a re-audit only needs the new ones. A `derived` item must name at least one target that is itself owner-backed; a chain of derivations is followed back to an owner turn.

## Refusals

Both refusals name each offending item, and nothing is recorded:

- `item_provenance_missing`: an item has no owner-backed mapping and no valid declaration. Each named item carries a `code`: `no_mapping`, `no_owner_ref` (its mappings cite only assistant, machine-injected or unreadable turns), or `derived_source_not_owner_backed` (declared derived, but none of its sources is owner-backed).
- `item_provenance_invalid`: a declaration names an unknown or dropped item (`provenance_item_unknown`), declares the same item twice (`provenance_item_duplicate`), is derived with an empty `from` (`provenance_derived_from_empty`), or is agent-added without a reason (`provenance_reason_empty`). These structural problems are checked first; the coverage refusal above is only reached when there are none.

The repair is either a better mapping (cite the owner turn that actually asked for it) or an honest declaration. Do not cite your own summary of the owner's words as if it were the owner: your turns never count.

## Older plans: the grandfather ratchet

A plan whose earlier activation audits predate provenance is not refused. Its re-audit is recorded with `enforced:false` and the unresolved items are returned as a warning, and the lifecycle gate still accepts it. The ratchet engages on its own: the first re-audit in which EVERY item resolves is recorded `enforced:true`, and every audit after an enforced one is enforced too (`activation-item-provenance.ts`, where `legacy` is computed). So bring an old plan under the rule by declaring its unbacked items; there is no flag to flip.

## Items added after activation

For a plan whose latest audit is enforced, the conversation activation gate (`plans:start`, and ready/active transitions) refuses with `item_provenance_unresolved` while any current non-dropped item was not resolved by that audit, naming the items. Re-audit after adding items; the new ones need an owner mapping or a declaration like any other.

## Where the owner sees it

The `plans.provenance` sync query returns a label per current item, the quoted source turns with speaker and origin verdict, the forward mappings with rejected and open requests first, and the audited versus current plan revision with the items the audit has not seen. The plan detail view renders it without expanding anything: a chip on every item, a "What you asked for" list, and a staleness line. Only an affirmative owner verdict is labelled "Your words".

## Pitfall: classifying a long pasted turn from its head alone

A classifier fed only the first N characters of a turn cannot see the closing tag of a paste wrapper, so a long machine-injected paste looked like owner typing. The provenance resolver therefore reads the turn's tail as well as its head (WI-10004057). If you write another consumer of turn origin, give it both ends of the text.
